sources.entry: Build Snake using only JavaScript, HTML & CSS

summary.title: Think like a programmer: How to build Snake using only JavaScript, HTML & CSS
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a playable Snake game in a single HTML file using a canvas, plain JavaScript and a little CSS, while practicing problem decomposition and debugging a direction-reversal bug.
takeaways: Set up a canvas element in one HTML file and draw on it with the 2D context in JavaScript.
Represent the snake as an array of coordinates, move it by unshifting a new head and popping the tail, and grow it when it eats food.
Drive movement with a setTimeout-based main loop and change direction on arrow keydown events, blocking immediate reversal.
Handle game over with self-collision and wall checks, and track score in a div.
Reproduce a bug step by step and fix it by limiting direction changes to one per tick.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a Snake game in one snake.html file, starting from a blank canvas and adding a snake drawn from a coordinate array, movement via a head-add and tail-remove routine, and a timed main loop. It then adds arrow-key direction control, random food placement, growth, a score display, and game-over checks for self-collision and walls. A final section reproduces an unexpected-ending bug (quick key presses causing a reversal) and fixes it with a changingDirection flag; a small CSS style block centers the game on screen. Code is shown inline throughout, with a short conclusion.
